story.title: Trump Appoints Stephen Miller as Chief of Staff Following Midterm Defeat
story.summary: Donald Trump has appointed Stephen Miller as his new chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles. Miller, known for his hardline stance on immigration and as a key architect of Trump's mass deportation policies, is expected to reinforce Trump's agenda following a disappointing midterm election. His appointment may lead to increased tensions with Congress as the administration prepares for upcoming challenges.

explore_lenses.label: What actually changed at the White House?
explore_lenses.title: Miller takes over; Wiles shifts roles
explore_lenses.summary: Trump announced that Stephen Miller will become White House chief of staff on November 9, 2026, replacing Susie Wiles. Wiles is slated to move to Trump’s political operation rather than leave the president’s orbit altogether.

claims.text: The White House announced Miller’s appointment as the 33rd chief of staff on November 6, 2026; reporting on Trump’s announcement says his start date is Monday, November 9.
Trump said Wiles would move to his political operation, and Wiles said her commitment to Trump and his mission would continue despite her changing role.
This is a White House staff appointment, not a Senate-confirmed cabinet nomination: federal law authorizes the president to appoint White House Office employees and prescribe their duties.

explore_lenses.label: Why does Miller’s promotion matter for immigration?
explore_lenses.title: A policy architect gains broader control
explore_lenses.summary: Miller already held senior White House policy and homeland-security roles, and the administration identifies him with its immigration agenda. The title change does not itself amend immigration law or an executive order, but it places a central policy adviser in the job that coordinates White House operations.

claims.text: Miller’s 2026 White House financial disclosure listed him as deputy chief of staff for policy and homeland security adviser; the White House’s July 2026 staff report likewise listed those roles.

Executive Order 14159 directs executive agencies to enforce immigration laws against inadmissible and removable noncitizens, expand coordination through Homeland Security Task Forces, and pursue detention capacity and certain state-local enforcement agreements, subject to law and available appropriations.

The White House characterized Miller as a driving force behind the administration’s border and domestic-policy record; House Majority Whip Tom Emmer praised him as a driver of the administration’s border policies.

explore_lenses.label: What congressional conflict could follow?
explore_lenses.title: Oversight becomes the immediate flashpoint
explore_lenses.summary: The reported Democratic midterm victories set up a changed congressional environment when the next Congress assembles. A leading House Oversight Democrat has explicitly tied Miller’s promotion to planned investigations, while administration allies say his selection reinforces Trump’s agenda.

claims.text: ABC News and TIME reported that Democrats won control of both the House and Senate in the 2026 midterms, preceding the staffing change.
The Twentieth Amendment provides that Congress assembles at noon on January 3 unless Congress sets another day, making January 3, 2027 the default start of the new Congress.

Rep. Robert Garcia, then the ranking Democrat on the House Oversight Committee, said Miller should “lawyer up” and said Oversight Democrats would investigate him and contest his policies in Congress and the courts.
Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio described Miller as a trusted, effective adviser and said they expected to work with him to advance Trump’s agenda.

story_report.summary: President Donald Trump named Stephen Miller as White House chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles, with Miller set to begin Nov. 9 after the Nov. 6 announcement. The move follows midterm elections in which Democrats reportedly won control of both the House and Senate. It places a senior adviser known for hardline immigration views and for serving as deputy chief of staff for policy and homeland security adviser at the center of White House operations as the administration prepares to work with a new Congress.

sections.heading: Susie Wiles Departure Accounts
sections.body: Trump said Wiles would shift to his political operation, while Wiles said her commitment to Trump and his mission would continue in her new role. But ABC News, citing unnamed sources, reported that she submitted her resignation after Trump blamed her for the midterm losses. The chief of staff position is a White House staff appointment under the president’s authority to appoint White House Office employees, rather than a Senate-confirmed Cabinet post.

sections.heading: Miller Immigration Policy Record
sections.body: Before his appointment, Miller’s financial disclosure and the White House staff report listed him as deputy chief of staff for policy and homeland security adviser. The administration has already directed agencies to enforce immigration laws against inadmissible and removable noncitizens, expand Homeland Security Task Force coordination, pursue detention capacity and seek certain state-local enforcement agreements, subject to law and available appropriations. The White House and House Majority Whip Tom Emmer portrayed Miller as a key driver of the administration’s border policies.

sections.heading: Congressional Scrutiny of Miller
sections.body: The new Congress is scheduled by default to assemble on Jan. 3, 2027, after Democrats reportedly captured both chambers in the midterms. Rep. Robert Garcia, then the ranking Democrat on the House Oversight Committee, said Oversight Democrats would investigate Miller and challenge his policies in Congress and in court. Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, meanwhile, called Miller a trusted and effective adviser and said they expected to work with him to advance Trump’s agenda.

unresolved.text: Public accounts differ over whether Wiles’ departure was a planned reassignment or followed her resignation after disputes over the midterm losses.
It is not yet clear whether Miller’s elevation will produce new immigration directives or operational changes, rather than tighter coordination of policies already in place.
The new Congress’s committee leadership, investigative priorities, potential requests for records or testimony, and the administration’s legal response have not been determined.

related_stories.title: ANC Faces Significant Defeat in South Africa's Local Elections
related_stories.summary: The African National Congress (ANC) is projected to receive around 30% of the vote in South Africa's recent local elections, marking its lowest electoral performance to date. With over 80% of ballots counted, the party's share is significantly lower than its results in previous elections, indicating a continued decline for the once-dominant political force. The election results are expected to lead to coalition negotiations in major cities like Johannesburg and Tshwane.

related_stories.title: Eisenkot Receives Mandate to Form Government Amid Crisis Concerns in Israel
related_stories.summary: Eisenkot, a political newcomer, has been formally tasked by President Isaac Herzog with forming a new government in Israel. He has 28 days to achieve this despite his bloc not holding a clear majority. Eisenkot emphasized the need for trustworthy leadership that represents all segments of society, amid warnings of a potential crisis under the current government led by Netanyahu.

related_stories.title: Gadi Eisenkot Assigned to Form New Israeli Government After Elections
related_stories.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has officially tasked former military chief Gadi Eisenkot with forming a new government following the inconclusive results of the October 28 elections. Eisenkot, who leads an anti-Netanyahu alliance, has up to six weeks to negotiate a coalition capable of securing a parliamentary majority. The process is expected to be challenging, with potential alliances being politically sensitive.
